calls.head: The Hurricanes should tilt the ice
calls.body: At 5-on-5, the Hurricanes have been one of the league’s best at getting more of the chances than they give up, and the Canucks the worst. The ice should tilt the Hurricanes’ way, even if goaltending and bounces have the final say on the score.

surprises.head: Carolina hardly hit anyone
surprises.body: Carolina usually hits more than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 49 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 107 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 45 games.

story.head: Deslauriers scores twice as the Hurricanes beat the Canucks
paras: Nicolas Deslauriers, who scores in about 1 game in 20, scored twice. It was a busy first period. Logan Stankoven struck first for the Hurricanes early in the period, but Linus Karlsson tied it up for Vancouver midway through the period. Nikolaj Ehlers restored the Hurricanes’ lead just under two minutes later. Jonathan Lekkerimäki made it 2-2 for Vancouver on the power play with just two seconds left in the first. Deslauriers put the Canes back ahead 3-2 early in the second, but Arshdeep Bains made it 3-3 for Vancouver midway through the period. Leevi Meriläinen stopped Sebastian Aho on a penalty shot late in the period, but that’s where Vancouver’s luck ran out. Deslauriers struck again early in the third to put the Hurricanes back ahead 4-3, and Ehlers struck again midway through the period to make it 5-3. Stankoven struck again into the empty net with just over two minutes left. Juuso Välimäki made his Hurricanes debut, after playing for the Mammoth, and picked up an assist. Three players had three-point nights: Jackson Blake with three assists, Ehlers with two goals and an assist, and Stankoven with two goals and an assist.

The Hurricanes drove the play, outshooting the Canucks 44-17, and the scoreboard caught up. Pyotr Kochetkov made 14 saves for the Hurricanes. Kochetkov has won all six of his starts this season. The Hurricanes moved to 8-2-1, climbing into first in the NHL in points. The Canucks are sixth in the Pacific. The Canucks are winless in eight (0-7-1).

items.text: The Hurricanes have beaten the Canucks six straight times, going back to the 2024-25 season.
The Hurricanes have won eight of their last ten.
Nicolas Deslauriers scored his first two goals of the season, his first since Apr 13, 2025 (38 games played since).
The Hurricanes have won both meetings this season.
